items.followUp: What is the difference between an opening tag and a closing tag in HTML?

rubric.why: Paired tags enclose content with an opening tag and a closing tag.
rubric.description: States that paired tags have an opening tag and a separate closing tag.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying both the opening and closing tags in a pair.

rubric.why: A singular tag stands alone and does not have a separate closing tag.
rubric.description: Distinguishes singular tags from paired tags by stating that they stand alone or lack a separate closing tag.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly describing a singular tag.

modelAnswer: Paired tags have an opening tag and a separate closing tag, with content between them.
A singular tag stands alone and has no separate closing tag.

items.followUp: Convert (45)₁₀ into binary by repeated division.

rubric.why: Repeated division by 2 produces the binary digits as remainders.
rubric.description: States that the decimal number is repeatedly divided by 2 and the remainders are recorded.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the repeated-division-by-2 method and recording the remainders.

rubric.why: The remainders must be read in reverse order to form the binary number.
rubric.description: States that the remainders are read from bottom to top.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving the correct order in which to read the remainders.

modelAnswer: Repeatedly divide the decimal number by 2 and record each remainder.
Read the remainders from bottom to top to obtain the binary number.
